description: StrataSight is a team of technology enthusiasts passionate about space, Earth science, AI, and innovation. We aim to turn NASA data into meaningful insights and develop creative solutions to real-world challenges. We welcome curious and motivated participants with skills in Python, AI/ML, data science, software development, GIS, data visualization, research, or UI/UX design.
summary:
StrataSight is a web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective.” It helps anyone ask a plain question about a place on Earth, such as whether the air is warming or soils are drying, then retrieve decades of real NASA and partner agency observations for that location.

The app answers the four questions the challenge requires: what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether the change is statistically significant. Results combine a clear verdict, charts, a world trend map, and a full statistical report that uses autocorrelation-aware Mann-Kendall testing, Sen’s slope with confidence intervals, and false-discovery control on multi-location maps. Every series shows its agency, product, and provenance. Nothing is simulated.

Users can also explore NASA satellite imagery on a 3D globe, compare places, and open an optional AI climatologist that explains findings in everyday language. StrataSight matters because Earth system change is uneven across regions, and trustworthy, accessible analysis turns open NASA data into decisions people can understand and defend.
